What comes up in Warners Bay

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table describes how these jobs generally go in this area. Your block may not match it, which is the reason for looking at it first.

Dig on low lying lakeside ground

Where the water table is close enough that the face will not stand on its own.

How it is handled
Battered back or supported rather than left vertical, with dewatering planned and pumps on site from the start.
What does it
Excavator with pumps, a batter or shoring designed for the condition.

Knockdown on a falling lakeside block

Established housing on ground that runs down towards the water.

How it is handled
Structure removed, then the cut benched from the high side with each level stable before the next.
What does it
Midi excavator able to work on a grade, tippers staged at the street.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Warners Bay

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Lakefront and lakeside blocks Where low lying ground affects excavation, drainage and what material can be reused.
  • A fall on many blocks Running down towards the water, which brings benching into the scope.
  • Established housing Mostly pre 1990, so the survey comes first.
  • Mine subsidence districts in parts of the area Worth confirming for a property before a design is fixed.

Warners Bay access varies street by street, from generous sloping blocks to tight lakefront lots with a single narrow approach. Near the water the ground is softer and that affects where plant can track more than it affects the demolition.

Warners Bay questions

What people ask before we start

Does being near the lake change the excavation?
Yes. Where the water table is close an open excavation does not stay dry, so dewatering and support are planned rather than discovered. It also affects what the material is suitable for if it is being reused on site.
Can you get plant onto a lakefront block?
Usually, but what size decides the programme. Where there is a single narrow approach the work goes to smaller plant with material moved out in stages.
Do you work around the lake as well as in Newcastle itself?
Yes. Charlestown, Warners Bay, Belmont and the surrounding suburbs are part of the same coverage, along with Maitland inland.
Does the asbestos work sit under your demolition licence?
No. Demolition licence AD214737 covers the structure. Removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists and clearance by an independent licensed assessor, because the assessor has to be independent of whoever did the removal. All of it is scheduled as a single job.
